items.name: terse
items.description: [![inth3shadows/terse MCP server](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/inth3shadows/terse/badges/score.svg)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/inth3shadows/terse)      - Transparent proxy that sits in front of any other MCP server and shrinks its tool output before it reaches the model. Lossless by default — a denser encoding of the same bytes, with a round-trip gate asserting an exact inverse, so nothing is dropped or summarised. Repeated calls to the same tool emit a delta against the prior result instead of the whole payload. Per-tool opt-in, no decode step, no model in the loop. `uv tool install terse-mcp` then `terse proxy -- <server>`

Attaches over `chrome.debugger` to the Chrome you're already logged into (cookies, MFA and SSO already done) and turns the live page into a short numbered interaction graph an agent can act on (`[03] button 'Sign In'`), with CSS selectors kept server-side and out of the model's context. Cross-identity tools (`compare_identities`, `replay`) flag a byte-identical response across two logged-in users as a cross-tenant IDOR, and `scan` maps the attack surface from the CLI. No LLM in the parse; 71% fewer tokens than Playwright's ARIA snapshot mode.

items.name: mcp-airlock
items.description: [![Shalimov04/mcp-airlock MCP server](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/Shalimov04/mcp-airlock/badges/score.svg)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/Shalimov04/mcp-airlock)      - Governance proxy in front of an MCP server. Each tool gets a risk tier per environment: read-only, forced dry run, dry run then human confirmation over a signed approve link, or straight through. The confirmation token is HMAC-signed and self-contained, so the proxy keeps no approval store, any replica can finish a confirmation, and each token is spent exactly once; a replay, a tampered argument or a bad signature is refused with a named rule. Blast-radius limits cap how many objects one call and one principal may touch per hour, every call writes a JSONL audit record before and after, and secrets are redacted on the way out. Python, MIT. `uvx mcp-airlock --policy policy.yaml --upstream <url>`
